answer: Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 44% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. Policies are written in thread, settled in summit, and dawn lists every payout. A farm hence faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. That bill is paid per identity, so 156 aliases cost 287 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
